cards.text: Friend, Jesus has just fed five thousand men with five loaves and two fish (Mark 6:41-44). Immediately after that, Jesus makes His disciples get into the boat. And I mean MAKES, friend, that's the word Mark uses.

cards.question: Jesus makes His disciples get into the boat and head across the water. Where does He send them?
Jesus climbs into the boat and sails to Bethsaida with His disciples.

cards.text: Jesus stays behind and sends the crowd off. After bidding them farewell, He goes up on the mountain.

cards.question: After bidding the crowd farewell, Jesus goes up on the mountain to ___.

cards.text: Evening comes, and the boat's in the middle of the sea while Jesus is alone on land. From there, He can see His disciples straining to row.

cards.question: From land, Jesus sees His disciples straining to row out on the sea. Why are they straining?

answers.text: The boat is taking on water
One of the oars has snapped

cards.text: Rowing into the wind is walking UP the down escalator, friend, and every stroke is WORK. Then, about the fourth watch of the night, Jesus goes out to them.

cards.question: About the fourth watch of the night, Jesus goes out to His disciples, ___ on the sea.

cards.text: Now here's the line that makes me stop mid-stamp: Mark says Jesus intended to pass by them. But the disciples see Him walking on the sea.

cards.question: The disciples see Jesus walking on the sea in the night. They cry out, thinking He's a ___.
Only a few of the disciples actually see Jesus out on the water.

cards.text: They're terrified, and I'm not judging, because last week I jumped at my own shadow on the oven door. MY OWN SHADOW, friend, but Jesus speaks up at once.

cards.question: Jesus speaks up at once to His terrified disciples out on the sea. What does He tell them?

answers.text: It's Me so don't be afraid

cards.text: Jesus says, "Take courage! It is I. Do not be afraid." Then He climbs into the boat with them.

cards.question: Once Jesus climbs into the boat with His disciples, the wind gets even stronger.

cards.text: The wind dies down, and the disciples are utterly astounded. Then Mark slows down to tell us why.

cards.question: Mark says the disciples are astounded because they hadn't understood about something from earlier that day. What?
Mark says the disciples' hearts had been hardened.

cards.text: They cross over, land at Gennesaret and moor the boat. Solid ground, friend, and I bet nobody in that boat complained about it.

cards.question: As soon as Jesus gets out of the boat at Gennesaret, the people there recognize Him.

cards.text: And then they RUN, friend. All through that whole region.

cards.question: People run through the whole region around Gennesaret. What do they carry to wherever they hear Jesus is?

cards.text: Villages, towns, countrysides, wherever He goes, they lay the sick in the marketplaces. Nobody ever ran across a whole region to find ME, because back in the junk drawer the only hand that came digging was looking for scissors.

cards.question: In the marketplaces, the people beg Jesus to let the sick touch just one thing. What is it?
And ___ who touched Jesus were healed.

findings.problem: The question asks 'Where does He send them?' The word 'send' tells the baker that Jesus isn't going with the disciples. That gives away the answer to card 3, which asks whether Jesus sails to Bethsaida with them.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: Part of the false statement 'Jesus climbs into the boat and sails ... with His disciples' is true later in the passage. Jesus climbs into the boat with them (Mark 6:51) and crosses over with them (Mark 6:53). Only 'to Bethsaida' makes the statement false, so a baker could argue it's true.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: The humor line 'Solid ground, friend, and I bet nobody in that boat complained about it' is mild and pleasant, not a real laugh. Also, the wind had already died down in Mark 6:51, so the relief at reaching land doesn't land.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: The right answer is people ('The sick on mats'), while the wrong answers are objects. 'Their fishing nets' is also silly: no one would run through a whole region carrying fishing nets to wherever Jesus was, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.
